findings.area: Shared rate gate / native PDF redirects
findings.finding: ctx.request.get(pdfUrl) uses automatic redirects outside browser ctx.route. Only the initial URL is reserved and the final response inspected; intermediate PDF redirects are not individually gated or inspected.
findings.recommendation: Disable automatic redirects for the request-context download, and explicitly reserve, inspect and record each redirect hop before following it. Preserve challenge/429 stop behavior on every response.
findings.current_scope: Portable live-method safety gap. Review did not establish an actual redirected rate-limit event in current retained evidence.
findings.followup_note: Current PDF loop uses maxRedirects0, reserves every hop, records hops and checks challenge/403/429 before following redirects. No independent network retest.

findings.finding: The lean root branch throws for non200 or visible Just-a-moment/Access-denied but does not persist stop-browser. The shared stop currently depends on a cf-mitigated response header; a headerless visible challenge can fail one target while run_browser continues with the next.
findings.recommendation: Classify visible access challenges separately from ordinary missing-route errors and persist the shared family stop before throwing; include Attention-required and equivalent challenge outcomes. Apply equivalent classification to API challenge responses.
findings.current_scope: Portable family-stop safety gap, not a claim that every HTTP404 must stop all targets.
findings.followup_note: Lean visible/root refusal now persists shared stop; API/organization403/429 paths also persist refusal. No network retest by independent reviewer.

findings.finding: Cached response reuse chooses the first Products/name, Jobs/latest and ClientContent response by URL substring. The current code verifies state/client name and visible ClientContent product, but does not assert job.ProductId===product.ProductID. The full-bootstrap path can therefore reuse a different publication response from the same municipality.
findings.recommendation: Filter cached responses to exact requested client/publication/product URL parameters and assert organization-to-product ClientID, job.ProductId-to-ProductID and visible ClientContent binding before TOC/content acquisition.
findings.current_scope: Default minimal path makes explicit requests and is narrower; full-bootstrap optional path and explicit Job binding remain underqualified. No wrong-current-city sample was demonstrated.
findings.followup_note: Current collector asserts lean organization/client equality, validates full-mode publication-name and query-client consistency, pins Jobs/latest and ClientContent to exact IDs and asserts job.ProductId. No wrong retained sample asserted.

findings.finding: The normalizer requires one requested DocID and nonempty text but does not require an acquired/no-access-stop receipt, validate raw samples against response hashes, or verify product/job identity linkage. The runner normalizes samples whenever samples.json exists even when acquisition status failed.
findings.recommendation: Bind normalized content to accepted raw API response evidence and product/job/source identity. Distinguish useful partial retained-source normalization from a successful standalone live acquisition; do not let a normalizer output alone promote a failed/access-stopped run to E2E pass.
findings.current_scope: Qualification-design gap. A failed native export can coexist with usable earlier legal API bytes; preserve those scopes separately instead of overstating or discarding them.
findings.followup_note: Current scripts/verify.py now checks both primary and supplemental raw acquisition bindings: HTTP200/acquired/noaccessstop, exact product/job/node queries, source bytes hashes, sample-content equality, executed source hashes and supplemental observed TOC membership. The normalizer guard remains complemented by the final read-only verifier.

findings.area: Native PDF source and currency qualification
findings.finding: The collector marks publisher_download passed for HTTP200+%PDF signature. inspect_pdf reads PDF structure and first selected pages but does not match sampled provision bodies or edition/banner text to the native PDF.
findings.recommendation: Keep byte acquisition success as a valid transport outcome, but label source/edition qualification separately or perform bounded sample/currency matching before claiming a source-matched export pass.
findings.current_scope: Actual native download bytes remain valid evidence; this is missing source/currency qualification, not an allegation of a wrong or synthetic PDF.
findings.followup_note: Current edition_check.py and Henderson edition-check evidence qualify native PDF first-page jurisdiction/state and supplement against observed API job metadata. Independent reviewer also read the actual native PDF first page locally and confirmed HENDERSON/NEVADA/SUPPLEMENT59. build_results.py explicitly excludes body-level correspondence/full current-law completeness, downgrades unmatched header editions to partial and records first-pages-only scope. Byte transport success is retained as a separate valid outcome.

findings.finding: The code computes sampleUrl but never navigates there. In lean mode application /dist/ assets are omitted, so rendered.html/png capture the bootstrap page rather than the selected substantive section.
findings.recommendation: Label these artifacts as bootstrap-shell evidence, or deliberately perform and qualify selected-section rendering. Keep API acquisition proof distinct from rendered substantive QA claims.
findings.current_scope: Documentation/receipt provenance correction; API-backed substantive sampling can still pass independently.
findings.followup_note: Receipt now explicitly labels lean screenshot as normal publisher shell and full-mode screenshot as unasserted page state. Substantive API evidence is distinguished.

findings.finding: LegalHTML adds no plain-text separator at td/th boundaries, so adjacent cell values concatenate in text/CSV (in-memory example: Unit+Rate becomes UnitRate). It stores only one active table/row/cell, so nested tables overwrite outer state and lose outer metadata rows/tail cells. verify_table inspects only the first JSONL record.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit cell/row separators to plain text, use a stack or fail closed on nested tables, and qualify table-bearing records actually covered by DOM comparison. Scope any unsupported nested-table behavior explicitly.
findings.current_scope: Reproduced read-only in memory; no currently retained table-bearing live sample was found during this review scan, so no existing table damage is asserted. Original HTML remains recoverable.
findings.followup_note: Flat/nested parser fixes independently verified in memory. Final design explicitly scopes browser DOM QA to one supplemental record; no claim that all primary provisions have source-backed table QA. Queued live table QA outcome itself was not presumed by this source review.
